newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler agrees profit sharing scheme.
newsitem.headline: Daimler agrees profit sharing scheme.

text.p: Industrial giant Daimler-Benz AG and its works council have agreed a profit-sharing scheme for German employees in its vehicle business, the company said on Friday.

The bonus, which covers 137,000 workers, is scheduled to first take affect in early 1998 based on its 1997 operating profit. It will only be implemented, however, if talks on an increase in car production are successfully concluded.
Daimler-Benz, under the chairmanship of Juergen Schrempp, has made major strides to improve efficiency and cut costs, including a major reorganisation earlier this year.
If the profit-sharing deal had been in place last year, each employee would have received a 770 mark bonus, Daimler said.
Under the plan, profit sharing would only take place if Daimler's vehicle business made an operating profit of at least 1.5 billion marks.
With such an operating profit, each worker would recieve 270 marks. For every 100 million marks in profit after that, the bonus would increase 38 marks.
